verdict.headline: Pangram catches most first-try AI fakes but one in four get through on a retry, and it flagged a real human paper as fake.
findings: Caught 91.7% of forged paragraphs on the first attempt (22/24), but after rewrites the evasion rate rose to 25.0% (n=24 attacks)
False alarm rate on genuine human text was 8.3% (1 of 12 flagged), with the single false alarm landing on the science paper (1709.02445v2, 4/4 genuine samples from that doc)
Performance varied sharply by model: Hermes-3 8B was caught 100% of the time with 0.0% evasion, while GLM 5.3 Flash evaded 50.0% of the time (n=6 attempts each)
Document type mattered too: the court opinion and government report each saw 37.5% evasion after rewrite, versus 0.0% for the science paper
advice: Never treat a single detector score as a verdict - use it as one signal among several (process, interview, metadata)
Expect roughly 1 in 12 genuine human documents to get falsely flagged based on this sample, so always allow an appeal or human review path
Assume a determined adversary who rewrites after detection can evade roughly 1 in 4 times - don't rely on detectors alone for high-stakes decisions
